prompt: Why do many coasts get two high tides a day instead of one?

options.text: The Moon pulls Earth’s near and far sides with different strengths
The Sun creates the second high tide every day
Wind pushes the water back at night

explanation: The difference in pull between the near side, the center and the far side of Earth raises two bulges. Earth rotates beneath them.
misconception: The Sun does affect tides, but the second high tide would exist without it: it comes from the difference in the Moon’s pull.

prompt: When do the strongest tides, spring tides, happen?

options.text: When the Sun, Earth and Moon line up, at new and full Moon
At first and last quarter Moon

explanation: With all three aligned, solar and lunar tides add up. That happens twice a month, in every season.
